title: Flip CONFIG_DIR_NAME to .ultraworkers, with the mandatory W6a project-root pin
one_line: Point new writes at ~/.ultraworkers while every project directory named .omp keeps being read, by splitting the project-level directory name into its own constant that is deliberately never renamed.
user_visible_effect: New config, sessions and settings are written under ~/.ultraworkers instead of ~/.omp. A user whose home root is still only ~/.omp keeps every session, setting and install-id exactly as-is and sees no error. Every project that has a .omp directory committed in its repo — including the 'This project (.omp/rules)' scope in the rules editor — keeps resolving to that .omp, unchanged. What the user never sees is the failure this work exists to prevent: no error, no warning, no missing config, just a silent re-login because the project directory stopped being found.

test_contract: Defends two things. (1) PROJECT_DIR_NAME is pinned to ".omp" independently of CONFIG_DIR_NAME, and the two constants have DIVERGED — that divergence is the contract, and if they ever become equal again someone has flipped the project root too. (2) A project directory that already contains a committed .omp/ is still what getProjectAgentDir() resolves to, even when a directory named after the NEW home root sits right next to it. What the consumer sees if this regresses: a user opens a repo they have been using for months, their project settings, rules and skills silently disappear, no error is printed, and the app behaves as if freshly installed. Secondary contract, in the legacy shim test: the compat surface exported from the legacy package root stays bound to the home-root constant and is not re-pointed at the pinned project constant — if it regresses, every third-party legacy extension resolves its config directory to a path that does not exist.

gate: All of the following, and they are genuinely falsifiable: (1) `bun run check:ts` is green. (2) The three new/updated utils tests pass. (3) packages/coding-agent/test/modes/controllers/omfg-controller.test.ts passes UNCHANGED — it asserts the literal paths <projectDir>/.omp/rules at lines 178,198,202,215,220 and the option label "This project (.omp/rules)" at line 15; if omfg-controller.ts:285 still read CONFIG_DIR_NAME after the flip, every one of those assertions fails. (4) packages/coding-agent/test/extensibility/legacy-pi-cli-exports.test.ts passes with the value pin replaced by the binding assertion. (5) `git grep -n 'CONFIG_DIR_NAME' -- 'packages/**/*.ts'` returns no project-root join: every remaining hit must be a HOME-root use, a comparison against the constant itself, or a re-export.
gate_can_fail: Yes, and in four distinct ways that were each verified against the real tree rather than assumed. (a) Forget dirs.ts:590 — getProjectAgentDir() returns a path nobody has data in, and dozens of existing project-scoped tests across packages/coding-agent/test go red. (b) Forget omfg-controller.ts:285 — omfg-controller.test.ts goes red on its literal .omp/rules path assertions, which is the only automated signal that this site exists. (c) Forget discovery/helpers.ts:47 — extensions-discovery.test.ts and advisor-toggle.test.ts go red. (d) Do nothing about the test in W6a at all — the flip is still caught by (a)-(c), but the new test is what makes the pin a stated decision rather than an accident nobody consciously made, and it is the only assertion that the two constants must stay DIVERGED. Separately verified: the harness note that `bun test` is blocked by a missing native addon is FALSE on this machine — `bun test packages/utils/test/dirs.test.ts` reports 6 pass / 0 fail and dirs-python-gateway.test.ts reports 2 pass / 0 fail, so the real test run is available as a gate.

effort: S for the main flip, S for W6a option (b) as specified here — but larger than the plan's claim of a single line. Real count: 1 line flipped in dirs.ts, 1 new constant, 3 call sites repointed (only 1 of which the plan names), 1 existing test's value pin relaxed, 1 new test, 1 do_not_rename row. Option (a) from the plan (dual-read at the project level) remains M and should not be chosen without a decision.
risk: The single most likely way to get this wrong is treating W6a as a one-line change at dirs.ts:590 because that is what the plan says, and leaving omfg-controller.ts:285 and discovery/helpers.ts:47 reading CONFIG_DIR_NAME. Both are product-level project-root reads that the plan's W6a analysis missed entirely; both fail silently — project-scope rules resolve to an empty directory and project-local skills/agents discovery returns nothing, with no error and no missing-config warning. The second-most-likely mistake is leaving the literal ".omp" assertion in legacy-pi-cli-exports.test.ts:14, which turns a survivable migration into a red test nobody can explain. The third is flipping CONFIG_DIR_NAME before repointing the call sites, which creates a window where a partial commit silently breaks project directories.
open_questions: Where does do_not_rename.tsv actually live? The plan's §2.3 defines it as a 17-row table but never names a file path, and scripts/rename/ does not exist yet. This spec proposes scripts/rename/do_not_rename.tsv alongside W8b's disposition.tsv. Confirm with the W7/W8b owner — a registry in the wrong place is one W7 will not read, and W7's sed pass is what makes the exclusion set load-bearing.

Should W6 wait for W4 and W5 to be used in a real release, or is 'shipped and CI-green' enough? The plan says both must have shipped AND been used in a real release. That is a calendar dependency no test can discharge, and it is the one gate that cannot be automated.

Is the string 'This project (.omp/rules)' in the omfg rules editor a literal in the controller, or derived from a constant? If literal, it correctly stays '.omp' and the user-visible label is unchanged; if it is built from a renamed constant it would drift from the on-disk path. Step 5 tells the implementer to check this, but the answer should be recorded in the commit message so a later reader knows it was deliberate.
